syllabus.name: AQA GCSE Biology (8461), Paper 1, Higher tier

units.title: Cell structure and microscopy
points: Label the structures of animal, plant and bacterial cells and state their functions
Compare eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells and give examples of each
Explain how cell specialisation and differentiation suit a cell's function
Calculate magnification, image size and real size in µm and mm
Describe how to use a light microscope to observe and draw cells (RP1)
Compare light and electron microscopes in resolution and magnification
Explain order of magnitude and standard form for cell sizes
Describe how sperm, nerve and muscle cells are adapted

units.title: Cell division and stem cells
points: Describe the stages of the cell cycle including interphase and mitosis
Explain why mitosis produces genetically identical diploid cells
Describe how the cell cycle is used in growth and repair
State the sources of embryonic and adult stem cells, and plant meristems
Evaluate the uses and risks of stem cells in medicine and therapy
Calculate the number of cells after repeated mitotic division

units.title: Transport in cells
points: Explain diffusion in terms of particle concentration and temperature
Describe factors affecting the rate of diffusion and give examples
Explain osmosis in terms of water potential across a partially permeable membrane
Explain the effects of osmosis on animal and plant cells
Investigate osmosis using plant tissue masses (RP3)
Calculate percentage change in mass and identify the isotonic point
Describe active transport and give examples such as root hair cells and the gut
Compare diffusion, osmosis and active transport

units.title: Principles of organisation and enzymes
points: Describe the levels of organisation from cells to organ systems
Explain how digestive enzymes break down carbohydrates, proteins and lipids
State where amylase, protease and lipase are produced and act
Explain the effect of temperature on enzyme activity and denaturation
Explain the effect of pH on enzyme activity and the optimum pH
Use the lock-and-key model to explain enzyme specificity
Describe how to test foods for sugars, starch, protein and lipids (RP4)
Investigate the effect of pH on amylase activity (RP5)

units.title: The circulatory system
points: Label the heart: atria, ventricles, valves, aorta and vena cava
Describe the double circulatory system and its advantages
Explain how the heart rate is controlled by the pacemaker
Describe arteries, veins and capillaries and relate structure to function
Describe the composition of blood and the function of each component
Explain how stents, statins and artificial valves treat heart disease
Calculate cardiac output from heart rate and stroke volume

units.title: Health and disease
points: Define health and describe causes of ill health
Describe risk factors for non-communicable disease, e.g. cancer and CHD
Explain how lifestyle and genetic factors interact in disease
Describe how benign and malignant tumours form
Interpret data on disease risk factors and correlations

units.title: Plant organs and transport
points: Describe the tissues of a leaf and their functions
Explain how the root hair cell and xylem are adapted for water uptake
Describe transpiration and factors affecting its rate
Explain translocation in the phloem and the role of sieve tubes
Label the structures of a leaf, stem and root from a diagram

units.title: Communicable diseases
points: State that communicable diseases are spread by pathogens: bacteria, viruses, fungi, protists
Describe measles, HIV and tobacco mosaic virus symptoms and spread
Describe salmonella and gonorrhoea and how their spread is controlled
Describe rose black spot and malaria, including the vector
Explain how pathogens cause damage and how diseases are transmitted
Suggest ways to reduce the spread of disease

units.title: Human defence and vaccination
points: Describe the non-specific defences: skin, mucus, cilia, stomach acid
Explain the role of white blood cells in phagocytosis and antibody production
Explain how vaccination gives immunity and prevents epidemics
Describe the immune response to a first and second infection
Evaluate the use of vaccination and herd immunity, including risks

units.title: Drugs, antibiotics and drug development
points: Describe the discovery and development of new drugs from plants
Explain how antibiotics work and why resistance develops
Explain why antibiotics do not work on viruses and painkillers only treat symptoms
Describe the stages of clinical trials including placebo and double-blind
Evaluate benefits and risks of antibiotic use and drug testing

units.title: Monoclonal antibodies (Higher)
points: Describe how monoclonal antibodies are produced from a single cell
Explain how monoclonal antibodies are used in pregnancy tests
Describe their use in cancer treatment and diagnosis
Evaluate the advantages and problems of monoclonal antibody therapy

units.title: Plant disease and defences
points: Describe plant diseases and their detection methods
Identify common plant diseases from symptoms and data
Describe physical, chemical and mechanical plant defences
Explain plant defences and adaptations such as thorns and poisons

units.title: Photosynthesis and limiting factors
points: Write the word and balanced equation for photosynthesis
Explain how light, temperature and CO2 limit the rate of photosynthesis
Interpret graphs of rate against light intensity and other factors
Explain how glucose is used: respiration, starch, cellulose, amino acids
Investigate the effect of light intensity on pondweed (RP6)
Explain how photosynthesis was investigated historically
Use limiting factor graphs to predict rate changes

units.title: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration
points: Write the equation for aerobic respiration and state energy uses
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration in muscles and yeast
Explain the effects of exercise on the body and response to oxygen debt
Describe metabolism and the role of the liver in lactic acid breakdown
Interpret data on respiration and exercise response

syllabus.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL

units.title: Sequences and series
points: Use arithmetic and geometric sequences, nth term and sum formulas
Use sigma notation and apply the binomial theorem
Find sums of finite arithmetic and geometric series
Solve financial problems: compound interest, depreciation, annuities
Use counting principles, permutations and combinations
Solve problems on the binomial expansion with rational indices

units.title: Number and algebra
points: Apply laws of exponents with rational exponents
Solve exponential equations using logarithms
Use the laws of logarithms, including change of base
Solve logarithmic and exponential inequalities
Sketch and analyse exponential and logarithmic graphs
Solve equations of the form a^x = b using logarithms

units.title: Proof and mathematical induction
points: Use direct proof and proof by contradiction
Use proof by counterexample
Prove statements by mathematical induction
Apply proof to divisibility and inequality statements
Distinguish when each method is appropriate
Construct rigorous arguments with clear reasoning

units.title: Permutations
points: Counting principles and permutations and combinations
Binomial coefficients and their relationship to combinations
Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions
Use partial fractions in integration and series work

units.title: Complex numbers
points: Perform arithmetic with complex numbers in Cartesian form
Find modulus, argument, conjugate and reciprocal
Use polar (trigonometric) and exponential forms
Multiply and divide complex numbers in polar form
Use De Moivre's theorem to find roots and powers
Solve polynomial equations with real coefficients, including conjugate roots
Represent complex numbers on an Argand diagram

units.title: Systems of linear equations
points: Solve 3x3 systems using row reduction / elimination
Identify unique, infinite and no-solution cases
Use matrices or technology to solve systems
Interpret geometric meaning of solutions for lines and planes
Apply partial fractions to rational expressions
Solve linear equations with polynomial identity methods

units.title: Functions and graphs
points: Find domain, range, inverse and composite functions
Use the factor and remainder theorems
Find sums and products of polynomial roots
Sketch rational functions with asymptotes and intercepts
Identify odd, even and self-inverse functions
Use the modulus function and solve inequalities
Transform graphs: translations, stretches, reflections
Solve equations graphically and with technology

units.title: Functions
points: Use the discriminant to determine the nature of roots
Complete the square and find vertex, axis of symmetry
Solve quadratic inequalities
Find the roots of polynomials, including multiplicity
Solve equations reducible to quadratic form

units.title: Triangle trigonometry
points: Use the sine and cosine rules and area formula
Solve problems using bearings and 3D figures
Use reciprocal trigonometric ratios (sec, cosec, cot)
Use Pythagorean and quotient identities
Solve trigonometric equations with compound angles
Apply inverse trigonometric functions and their domains

units.title: Circular functions and identities
points: Convert between degrees and radians and use arc length and sector area
Use the unit circle and reference angles
Apply compound and double angle identities
Use symmetry to simplify and solve trigonometric expressions
Sketch trigonometric functions and identify transformations
Solve trigonometric equations in given intervals

units.title: Further trigonometry
points: Define and use inverse trigonometric functions, including their domains and ranges
Solve equations using inverse trigonometric functions
Apply the double angle identity for tangent
Apply compound angle identities to solve equations

units.title: Vectors
points: Use vector notation, addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication
Find magnitude and unit vectors in 2D and 3D
Compute scalar (dot) product and cross product
Find angles between vectors
Solve equations of lines and planes
Find intersections and shortest distances involving lines and planes

units.title: Statistics and probability
points: Use descriptive statistics: mean, median, quartiles, standard deviation, IQR
Interpret box plots, histograms and cumulative frequency
Calculate probabilities using sample spaces, Venn diagrams and tree diagrams
Apply conditional probability and independent events
Use Bayes' theorem
Solve problems with mutually exclusive and exhaustive events

units.title: Probability distributions
points: Use discrete random variables and probability mass functions
Find expected value, variance and standard deviation
Work with the binomial distribution and its conditions
Use the normal distribution and standardisation
Find probabilities using normal distribution and inverse normal
Use probability density functions and expectation algebra

units.title: Limits and differential calculus
points: Understand informal limits and convergence
Differentiate from first principles
Differentiate polynomial, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions
Apply product, quotient and chain rules
Differentiate inverse and reciprocal trigonometric functions
Use implicit differentiation
Apply L'Hopital's rule
Find tangent and normal equations

units.title: Applications of differential calculus
points: Analyse increasing/decreasing behaviour using first derivative
Find stationary points and classify them
Use the second derivative, concavity and points of inflection
Solve optimisation problems
Solve kinematics problems with displacement, velocity and acceleration

units.title: Integration
points: Find antiderivatives of standard functions
Compute definite and indefinite integrals
Use definite integrals for areas and volumes of revolution
Apply integration by substitution
Apply integration by parts
Apply partial fractions to integration

units.title: Calculus
points: Solve first-order differential equations by separation of variables
Use an integrating factor for linear first-order equations
Apply Euler's method to approximate solutions
Use Maclaurin series for standard functions
Use Taylor series and error bounds
Model real contexts with differential equations

units.title: Internal assessment: Mathematical exploration
points: Choose a topic with sufficient mathematical content for HL
Formulate a clear research question
Develop the mathematics coherently and rigorously
Justify methods and evaluate results
Include correct notation, graphs and diagrams
Reflect on limitations and possible extensions
Present a well-structured written report

syllabus.name: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind

units.title: The Cognitive Revolution
points: Trace how Homo sapiens came to dominate other human species
Explain the role of gossip and shared myths in large-group cooperation
Distinguish the Cognitive Revolution from later revolutions in the book's argument
Describe what archaeology and genetics say about early foragers

units.title: The Agricultural Revolution
points: Explain the book's argument that farming was 'history's biggest fraud'
Describe the costs of agriculture for health, diet and workload
Follow how surplus food supported elites, states and written records
Weigh the counterarguments to the book's luxury-trap thesis

units.title: The Unification of Humankind
points: Explain money as a system of shared trust
Trace how empires spread common cultures and norms
Describe religion's role in unifying large populations
Show how commerce, empire and religion wove separate worlds together

units.title: The Scientific Revolution
points: Explain the discovery of ignorance as a driver of modern science
Link science, European imperialism and capitalism
Describe how credit and trust in the future fuelled growth
Assess the book's claim that progress and happiness are not the same

units.title: The End of Homo Sapiens
points: Summarise the book's speculations on genetic engineering and cyborgs
Discuss the open questions it raises about the future of our species
Compare these projections with the book's own earlier arguments

units.title: Ethical and Professional Standards

points: Compute present and future values for lump sums and annuities

units.title: Economics: Microeconomics
points: Analyse demand and supply shifts and market equilibrium

units.title: Economics
points: Interpret national income accounting and GDP measures

Explain exchange rate regimes and currency exchange determination
Describe international trade theories and trade restrictions
Summarise geopolitical and capital flow considerations for economies

units.title: Financial Statement Analysis
points: Describe the roles and elements of the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement

Trace how transactions flow through the core financial statements
Apply general accounting principles such as accrual and revenue recognition

units.title: Corporate Issuers
points: Evaluate capital budgeting projects using NPV, IRR and payback
Compute and interpret weighted average cost of capital
Describe capital structure theories and leverage effects
Explain corporate governance, ownership structures and stakeholder relations
Analyse business models, working capital management and short-term liquidity
Describe capital raising for public and private companies

units.title: Portfolio Management
points: Explain the portfolio approach and investor characteristics
Compute portfolio expected return and risk
Interpret diversification, covariance and correlation
Describe risk aversion, mean-variance optimisation and efficient frontier
Explain risk management, portfolio planning and the investment policy statement

units.title: Equity Investments
points: Describe market organisation, structure and trading mechanics
Compare order types, execution and market regulation basics
Explain market efficiency and its implications
Compare security market indices and their construction
Apply equity valuation concepts of intrinsic value, price multiples and present value models
Describe company analysis and industry analysis fundamentals

units.title: Fixed Income
points: Describe fixed income instruments and issuers
Explain features of coupon bonds, floating rate and money market instruments
Compute bond prices, yields and yield measures
Explain yield curve shapes and term structure theories
Analyse interest rate risk, duration and convexity
Describe securitisation and fixed income asset classes

units.title: Derivatives
points: Describe forwards, futures, options and swaps and their payoff profiles
Interpret futures pricing and forward pricing basics
Apply option pricing basics: intrinsic value, put-call parity, binomial and Black-Scholes intuition
Explain uses of derivatives: hedging, arbitrage and speculation

units.title: Alternative Investments
points: Describe hedge funds, private equity, real estate, commodities and infrastructure
Explain fee structures and incentive alignment in alternative investments
Describe diversification, liquidity and valuation issues of alternatives
